slides.title: What makes a gadget
slides.text: A gadget has sensors and inputs that collect data, a processor, outputs, maybe storage and a connection, and power.

slides.title: Sensors
slides.text: A sensor measures the world: light, motion, sound, moisture. A plant waterer needs a moisture sensor to know when the soil is dry.

slides.title: Tradeoffs
slides.text: Every part costs money, battery and space. Wireless lets a gadget move freely but uses more battery than a cable. That is a tradeoff.

slides.title: A step counter
slides.text: The brief says: small, cheap, lasts all day. Pick only the parts the brief needs.

slides.title: Users decide what is next
slides.text: A gadget is finished when people can use it. Read what users say, and make that your next improvement.

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Inside the Machine at Design a Gadget and complete 3 briefs. Watch the cost, battery and size meters as you add each part.
